chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban narrated to us in the year three and seventy of the two hundred, saying: Ali ibn Sayf ibn Umayra narrated to us, saying: Abban ibn Uthman narrated to us from Humran ibn A'yun, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah about the Imams, and he said: 'He who denies one of the living has denied the dead.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the sixth Imam
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: The Imams, specifically the twelve infallible leaders in Shia theology

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of denying one of the living Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) serves as a foundational proof for the unbroken chain of Imamate, asserting that the living Imam embodies the same divine authority as his predecessors. By equating the denial of a living Imam with that of the deceased, it underscores the theological necessity of recognizing the current Imam during the Minor and Major Ghebah, ensuring the continuity of divine guidance. This statement was particularly significant for early Shia communities navigating periods of political obscurity and doubt regarding the active presence of the Imams.
